To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CuO nanoparticles (NPs), microparticles (particles), and ions (ions) induced oxidative stress and membrane perturbation, and the metabolic response was similar for particles and ions, while the toxicity of particles was particle size-specific.

(1) CuO NPs, MPs, and Cu ions induced similar oxidative stress and lipid membrane damage, and the corresponding metabolic responses were similar, (2) CuO N/Ps and ions caused different responses in the fatty acids oxidation, and (3) CuO NMs caused higher accumulation of fatty acids at 1 μg/L than ions, and caused lower accumulation of fatty acids, but higher accumulation of fatty acid oxidation products at 10 μg/L, than ions

(1) CuO NPs, CuO MPs and dissolved Cu ions caused different metabolic changes in C. vulgaries, and (2) CuO NPS and MPs had similar effects as Cu ions in most metabolic pathways, but caused specific metabolic changes in some pathways.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CuO NPs are no more toxic than CuO MPs and dissolved Cu ions to C. vulvaris.

CuO particles and Cu ions cause oxidative stress and membrane damages in C. vulgaries through the same mechanisms, while CuO particles cause more oxidative stress than Cu ions at low concentrations and less oxidative stress at high concentrations.
CuO NPs are not more toxic than CuO MPs to C. vulvaris, which is different from the case of CuO NMs and CuO MNPs to Daphnia magna.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CuO NPs have no specific effects on C. vulgalris metabolism, and the toxicity of Cu ions is the major factor for CuO NPs' toxicity.
the toxicity of Cu is mainly caused by Cu ions, but CuO NPs/MCs can also cause additional toxicity due to particle-specific toxicity.

the metabolic responses of C. vulvaris to CuO NPS were similar to those to CuO MPs and ions, but the particle-specific toxicity from CuO NPs was the accumulation of more fatty acid oxidation products at low concentration and less fatty acids oxidation products at high concentration.

the toxicity of Cu-containing NPs is mainly caused by Cu ions, and that NPs and MPs have no nanoparticle-specific toxicity.
